note: Authored craft-instruments-daily.yml from a spec naming the schedule, the corpora-first ordering and the emptiness gate. Structure correct. Three gate repairs: no top-level `name:`; action refs pinned to SHAs where this tree standardised on tags (113 uses of actions/checkout@v7 vs 7 of that SHA, and its setup-python pin was a v5 where the tree is on v7); and — the one that mattered — the emptiness-gate pattern was `([1-9][0-9]*) packs scanned` while the instrument actually prints `packs scanned: 84`, number AFTER a colon, so the gate could never match and would have warned on EVERY run forever.

Blind cross-family refutation. Its BLOCKER was real and is the same defect this squad fixed in lane 3 and then reintroduced by copying a sibling's shape: `TOTAL="$(bash suite | sed ...)"` under set -euo pipefail kills the step before the 'printed no TOTAL line' branch can run, so that branch is dead code on the only path it exists for. Also real: the pipefail comment claimed to detect a failed pipe in a step containing no pipes. Its permissions finding and its fixtures finding were both reasoning on a FALSE PREMISE I had put in the review prompt — I wrote that correction_tax 'queries GitHub'; its docstring opens 'Read-only against `git log`'. That false premise is what makes this review valuable in an unexpected direction: chasing it down surfaced a BLOCKER of my own making, because a `git log --since` window on the default shallow checkout is empty and the script deliberately exits 1 rather than report a share over it.
Out of credits across the whole Codex seat.
